lessons.title: Psychological / Emotional Bullying
lessons.description: A short video on emotional harm and getting support.
lessons.longDescription: Watch a short video on psychological and emotional bullying, then read the key points below. Repeated intimidation, humiliation, or threats can hurt even when there are no visible injuries.
learningObjectives: Recognize psychological and emotional bullying: repeated intimidation, humiliation, threats, and coercion.
Understand how this harm affects a student even when there are no visible injuries.
Name safe steps: do not blame the person, encourage them to tell a trusted adult, and seek Guidance Office support.
keyTakeaways: Emotional harm is real harm, and it deserves to be taken seriously.
Bullying is never the victim's fault, and no one has to face it alone.
Tell a trusted adult or the Guidance Office. Support is available.

lessons.title: Social / Relational Bullying
lessons.description: A short video on exclusion, rumors, and belonging.
lessons.longDescription: Watch a short video on social and relational bullying, then read the key points below. Social bullying harms friendships and a sense of belonging, and that harm is real.
learningObjectives: Recognize social bullying: deliberate exclusion, spreading rumors, and turning a group against someone.
Explain why leaving someone out on purpose is bullying, even when nothing physical happens.
Name safe steps: include the person, refuse to spread rumors, and tell a trusted adult.
keyTakeaways: Social and relational bullying harms belonging and friendships. It is real harm.
Do not spread rumors or join a group that is targeting someone.
Include others, and tell a trusted adult when it continues.

lessons.title: Physical Bullying
lessons.description: A short video showing what physical bullying looks like and what to do.
lessons.longDescription: Watch a short video on physical bullying, then read the key points below. Physical bullying uses physical actions to hurt, intimidate, or frighten another person.
learningObjectives: Recognize what physical bullying looks like at school.
Explain why safety comes first and why you should not physically intervene.
Name the adults or offices you can tell when it happens.
keyTakeaways: Physical bullying is repeated physical harm or intimidation; it is never acceptable.
Do not fight back or put yourself at risk — move to a safe place and get help.
Report it to a teacher, adviser, or the Guidance Office.

lessons.title: What is bullying?
lessons.description: Learn the basics and recognize harmful behavior.
lessons.longDescription: Learn how to recognize bullying, why it matters, and how to respond safely when you see it.
learningObjectives: Explain what bullying is and why repetition and power imbalance matter.
Recognize the most common forms of bullying.
Describe a safe first step when bullying happens.
keyTakeaways: Bullying is repeated harmful behavior; not every disagreement is bullying.
Everyone deserves respect, safety, and support.
Telling a trusted adult is a strong and safe step.

lessons.title: Being a helpful bystander
lessons.description: Safe ways to support someone who is being bullied.
lessons.longDescription: Bystanders can make a difference without putting themselves in danger. Learn safe ways to support a classmate.
learningObjectives: Identify safe ways to support a classmate who is being bullied.
Explain why joining in or forwarding harmful content makes things worse.
Name adults or offices that can help.
keyTakeaways: Do not join in, laugh along, or share harmful content.
Support the person and include them.
Tell a trusted adult when you see repeated harm.

lessons.title: Staying safe online
lessons.description: Think before you post, share, comment, or forward.
lessons.longDescription: Cyberbullying can follow students beyond school hours. Learn simple online safety habits and how to respond safely.
learningObjectives: Apply simple rules before posting or forwarding content.
Explain how to save evidence and seek help safely.
keyTakeaways: Pause before posting or forwarding hurtful content.
Protect your personal information and use privacy tools.
Block, report, and tell a trusted adult when it is safe to do so.
